catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.summary: A collection of publications organized by theme and schema
catalog.description: A catalog represents a curated collection of publications that can be organized by themes and schemas. It serves as the main organizational unit for content, allowing administrators to group related publications together and make them accessible through a unified interface. Catalogs can be public or private and can be associated with specific organizations.

listed.title: Listed

status.title: Status

hasOoapi.description: Whether this catalog publishes its course/program/offering data via the Open Onderwijs API (OOAPI 5.0). Read by OoapiService::isOoapiEnabled() to gate every /api/catalogs/{slug}/ooapi/v5/* route, and by DirectoryService to advertise ooapiEndpoint. Without this declaration the catalog schema's hardValidation strips the key, the toggle in CatalogModal.vue is silently discarded on save, and the whole OOAPI capability is unreachable — see #847.

course.title: Course
course.summary: An OOAPI 5.0 course, materialized from a scholiq Course by the OpenConnector ooapi-catalog Synchronization
course.description: A course represents an educational offering published by an institution via the Open Onderwijs API (OOAPI 5.0). Course objects are written by OpenConnector's ooapi-catalog Synchronization target, consuming scholiq's DataExchangeJob (target: ooapi-catalog); OpenCatalogi never calls scholiq directly to produce this object. Once materialized, the object is rendered as an OOAPI 5.0 course resource via the x-ooapi schema annotation.

catalog.description: The OpenCatalogi catalog this materialized course belongs to. Set by the OpenConnector ooapi-catalog Synchronization target when writing the object, so a single shared course/program/offering schema (design.md D6) can still be scoped per institution's catalog the way DCAT scopes publications via catalog.registers/catalog.schemas.

listing.description: A listing provides a customizable view of publications within a catalog. It allows for the creation of specific publication collections based on filters, sorting, and presentation preferences. Listings can be used to create featured sections, topic-based collections, or any other organized view of publications.

publication.title: Publication
publication.summary: A single publication entry within the catalog
publication.description: A publication represents an individual piece of content within the catalog. It can be associated with themes and schemas, and is the primary unit of content that users can view and interact with. Publications can be linked to specific organizations and can be either public or private.

organization.description: Reference to the organization that owns this publication
organization.title: Organization

themes.description: List of themes associated with this publication
themes.title: Themes

publicationDate.description: Publication date (WOO/DIWOO) — when set to a date in the past, this publication is live and publicly accessible
publicationDate.title: Publication Date

depublicationDate.description: Depublication date (WOO/DIWOO) — when set and in the past, this publication is withdrawn from public access. A future value schedules automatic depublication via the OpenRegister published-predicate.
depublicationDate.title: Depublication Date

retentionCategory.description: Selectielijst / WOO information-category reference that keys the statutory retention term (RET-003).
retentionCategory.title: Retention Category

retentionTermMonths.description: Statutory retention term in months, counted from the publication date (RET-003).
retentionTermMonths.title: Retention Term (Months)

retentionAction.description: Action taken when the retention term expires: review (flag only), depublish (set depublicationDate), or archive (lifecycle transition) (RET-003).
retentionAction.title: Retention Action

retentionExpiresAt.description: Computed retention expiry = publication date + retentionTermMonths. May be manually overridden, in which case retentionNote is required (RET-003).
retentionExpiresAt.title: Retention Expires At

retentionNote.description: Legal basis or exception rationale for the retention decision; mandatory when retentionExpiresAt is manually overridden or extended (RET-003).
retentionNote.title: Retention Note

retentionLastEvaluatedAt.description: Idempotency marker recording the date the retention evaluation job last actioned this publication (RET-005).
retentionLastEvaluatedAt.title: Retention Last Evaluated At

status.description: Lifecycle status of the publication; the archived state retains the object internally while removing it from every public surface (RET-006).
status.title: Status

publiccode.title: Public code component
publiccode.summary: A software component described by a publiccode.yml file
publiccode.description: One harvested publiccode.yml. The identity of a component is its repository URL, not its name: names collide across forges and change on rebrand, while the URL is what the harvest actually dereferenced. `slug` is derived from the repository full name so a re-harvest UPDATES rather than duplicates — the flow engine has no synchronisation contracts yet, so idempotency has to come from a deterministic identifier.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the software component, as declared in publiccode.yml.

applicationSuite.title: Application suite
applicationSuite.description: The suite this component belongs to, when it is part of one.

url.title: Repository URL
url.description: Canonical repository URL. This is the component's IDENTITY — see the schema description.

landingURL.title: Landing page
landingURL.description: Public landing page for the software — the human-readable page a prospective user should be sent to. Deliberately separate from `url`: publiccode.yml treats the repository as the identity and the landing page as the front door, and for many components they are different sites.

softwareVersion.title: Version
softwareVersion.description: Latest released version, as the maintainer numbers it. Kept as a free-form string rather than parsed: publiccode.yml records whatever the project publishes, and forcing it into semver would silently rewrite versions that are dates or build numbers.

releaseDate.title: Release date
releaseDate.description: Date the version in `softwareVersion` was released (YYYY-MM-DD). Read together with that field this is what separates a maintained component from an abandoned one, so it is the main signal behind any recency facet.

logo.title: Logo
logo.description: Path or URL to the logo. Left as declared: publiccode.yml permits a repository-relative path, and resolving it to an absolute URL is the harvest's job, not the schema's.

platforms.title: Platforms
platforms.description: Platforms the software runs on. publiccode.yml reserves the values `web`, `windows`, `mac`, `linux`, `ios` and `android`, and allows free text for anything else — which is why this is not an enum: constraining it would reject valid harvested documents.

developmentStatus.title: Development status
developmentStatus.description: One of: concept, development, beta, stable, obsolete.

softwareType.title: Software type
softwareType.description: One of: standalone/mobile, standalone/iot, standalone/desktop, standalone/web, standalone/backend, standalone/other, addon, library, configurationFiles.

description.title: Descriptions by language
description.description: publiccode.yml nests descriptions per language code (description.en.shortDescription, …). Kept nested rather than flattened to one language: flattening would silently discard every other translation on write.

maintenanceType.title: Maintenance type
maintenanceType.description: One of: internal, contract, community, none.

maintainers.title: Maintainers
maintainers.description: Who to contact about this component. Flattened from two separate publiccode.yml lists — `maintenance.contractors` (organisations under contract) and `maintenance.contacts` (named people) — because a catalogue reader is asking one question, not two. The distinction survives in each entry's own fields.

legalLicense.title: Licence
legalLicense.description: SPDX identifier, as declared in legal.license.

legalRepoOwner.title: Repository owner
legalRepoOwner.description: Legal entity that owns the repository. Not the same question as who publishes or maintains the component — this is the party that can relicense or transfer it, which is what a reuse decision actually turns on.

localisationAvailableLanguages.title: Available languages
localisationAvailableLanguages.description: Languages the interface is already available in, as BCP 47 tags. Distinct from publiccode.yml's `localisation.localisationReady`, which only claims that translating it is possible — an empty list here with `localisationReady: true` means nobody has translated it yet.

publiccodeYmlVersion.title: publiccode.yml version
publiccodeYmlVersion.description: Which version of the standard the harvested file declared. Recorded because the mapping is version-sensitive: a v0.2 file and a v0.4 file put maintainers in different places.

harvestedFrom.title: Harvested from
harvestedFrom.description: The forge host the file came from (github.com, gitlab.com, codeberg.org). Recorded so a harvest can be re-run per forge, and so a component that disappears from one forge is not confused with one that never existed.

harvestedAt.title: Harvested at
harvestedAt.description: When this object was last written by a harvest. A component whose harvestedAt stops advancing is one the harvest no longer finds — which is information, not an error.

rawPubliccode.title: Raw publiccode.yml
rawPubliccode.description: The decoded file as harvested. Kept because the mapping above is lossy by construction: any field the standard adds, or any country extension we do not model, would otherwise be discarded silently at harvest time and be unrecoverable without re-fetching.

theme.title: Theme
theme.description: Themes are used to categorize publications within catalogs. They provide a way to group related publications together, making it easier for users to find content they're interested in. Themes can be hierarchical and can be used for navigation and filtering purposes.

link.description: Button/link text for the theme card
link.title: Link Text

url.description: Destination URL when clicking the theme card link
url.title: URL

icon.description: Icon identifier for the theme card
icon.title: Icon

isExternal.description: Whether the link opens in a new tab
isExternal.title: Is External

usageCounter.title: UsageCounter
usageCounter.description: Internal plumbing schema holding privacy-safe daily aggregate usage counters for publications: one object per (publication, date, kind). It stores ONLY a publication reference, a day, a kind (view/download), an integer count, and an optional catalog slug for roll-ups — no IP address, user agent, session id, referrer, or any request-derived attribute is ever stored (ANA-002). It is never published, is excluded from catalogs, sitemaps, DCAT, search, and federation, and is RBAC-restricted to the app and officer roles.

catalog.description: Catalog slug for roll-up labelling (not personal data)
catalog.title: Catalog

count.description: Non-negative aggregate count for this (publication, date, kind)
count.title: Count

wooAssessment.title: WooAssessment
wooAssessment.summary: A per-document openbaarheid assessment within a Woo disclosure batch
wooAssessment.description: A document-assessment object represents the openbaarheid (public disclosure) decision for a single document collected in a Woo disclosure batch: which weigeringsgronden (WOO Art. 5.1/5.2 refusal grounds) apply, any redaction instructions, and the resulting anonymized document when partially disclosed. Each assessment is linked to a Deck card via the consumed deck leaf so its status is reflected on the document queue board.

documentReference.description: Reference to the source document being assessed (id or path from the originating case system)
documentReference.title: Document Reference

fileName.description: The file name of the document being assessed
fileName.title: File Name

fileType.description: The file type (MIME type or extension) of the document being assessed
fileType.title: File Type

assessment.description: The openbaarheid assessment decision for this document
assessment.title: Assessment

weigeringsgronden.description: Selected WOO Art. 5.1/5.2 refusal ground article references (required when the assessment is "niet_openbaar")
weigeringsgronden.title: Weigeringsgronden

redactionInstructions.description: Free-text redaction instructions for a partially-disclosed (deels_openbaar) document
redactionInstructions.title: Redaction Instructions

anonymizedDocument.description: Reference to the anonymized/redacted version of the document, used for deels_openbaar publication
anonymizedDocument.title: Anonymized Document

caseReference.description: The Procest Woo-verzoek case reference this assessment belongs to
caseReference.title: Case Reference

assessedBy.description: The user id that made this assessment decision, or "system" when assessed without an active user session
assessedBy.title: Assessed By

assessedAt.description: Timestamp this assessment decision was made
assessedAt.title: Assessed At

wooBatch.title: WooBatch
wooBatch.summary: A Woo disclosure batch grouping the documents released for one Woo-verzoek case
wooBatch.description: A Woo disclosure batch represents one Woo-verzoek (Wet open overheid request) case moving through document collection, per-document assessment, review and publication to the public reading room. It is the OpenRegister-backed storage WooService reads and writes; the document queue itself is provisioned as a Deck board via the consumed deck leaf (ADR-022) rather than a bespoke queue table.

caseReference.description: The Procest Woo-verzoek case reference this batch belongs to
caseReference.title: Case Reference

deckBoardId.description: The Deck board id provisioned (or re-used) for this batch's document queue
deckBoardId.title: Deck Board ID

deckAvailable.description: Whether the Deck app was available when this batch was created; false means the document queue/board could not be provisioned
deckAvailable.title: Deck Available

documents.description: References to the document-assessment objects collected in this batch
documents.title: Documents

decisionLetter.description: The Woo decision letter (besluit) content or reference for this batch
decisionLetter.title: Decision Letter

inventoryList.description: The generated inventarislijst (document inventory list) content or reference for this batch
inventoryList.title: Inventarislijst

documentSummary.description: Derived per-status document assessment progress (counts, total, assessed, progress label); computed on read from the linked assessment objects, not independently authoritative storage
documentSummary.title: Document Summary

publishedAt.description: Timestamp the batch was published to the public reading room
publishedAt.title: Published At

publishedCount.description: Number of documents published to the reading room (openbaar + deels_openbaar assessments)
publishedCount.title: Published Count

wooPublication.description: The publication metadata recorded when this batch was published: decision date, request reference, category, document/published counts, besluit, inventarislijst, per-document listings and the reading-room URL
wooPublication.title: Woo Publication

updatedAt.description: Timestamp the batch was last updated
updatedAt.title: Updated At

createdBy.description: The user id that created this batch, or "system" when created without an active user session
createdBy.title: Created By
